source_en: End of rotation. Standard transit.
Scheduled transfer. Clearance is on file.
Shift handover. My relief is posted.
Extended patrol. I cross twice daily now.
Reassigned after the eastern incident. Routine.
Double rotations. Third crossing today.
Lockdown rotation. I go where sent.
Emergency order reassignment. Papers current.
Standard transit. Expect many more of us.
Resigned from service. Seeking factory work.
Bakery co-op bread round. Morning delivery.
First checkpoint ever. Explain the procedure.
Resting. Command cancelled patrols east.
Collecting my maternity leave papers.
Off duty for good. No more orders.
Ignoring the emergency order. I go anywhere.
Church volunteer. The state means nothing.
Visiting family. My unit can wait.
Let's make this quick. I have a post to get back to.
You going to stare, or are you going to check the papers?
Twice today already. You'd think they'd streamline this by now.
Still running the same process, I see. No questions. We'll both be happier.
Just do what you're supposed to do. I've been through many checkpoints today.
Papers. Stamp. Done. That's all this needs to be.
Good. See, that wasn't so hard, was it?
Faster than yesterday. You're learning, officer. Good.
Adequate. Keep it up, officer. Eyes forward.
I will be filing an incident report the moment I'm released.
Do you have any idea what rank you are detaining right now?
…Didn’t think a post like this would actually follow through…
For the record… I still don’t think… your paperwork… was in order…
Where are you coming from?
End of rotation. Eastern sector, twelve hours. That is all your form needs.
Perimeter sweep, extended east after the incident. Second crossing today. Read the memos.
Lockdown rotation. Command sends, I go. Sector designation is not for civilians.
Home leave. Two weeks at my mother's in Batumi. Unit's on stand-down.
The eastern post. Full staff, all quiet. Nothing has happened out there.
The barracks. I have always been posted alone. There is no unit.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
No. Next question, officer. I will not repeat myself.
None I must disclose to civilians. Double rotations. Men get tired. Move on.
Headaches. No sleep in three days. Not a symptom. It is the situation.
No. Twenty years in uniform and never once on the sick list. Stamp it.
None. We are back on single shifts. The whole unit sleeps fine.
None. Command ran full medicals this morning. Clear orders, clear chain.
This checkpoint runs three seconds slower than the eastern one. I timed it.
Civilian checkpoints waste more time than they save. Not a criticism. An observation.
The east post went quiet two days ago. Nobody told me why.
You are still at your post. Good. Some of them are not.
Orders are still orders when the chain of command is unclear. Proceed.
Many checkpoints today. This is the last one I recognize.
